title: 1980s physicists' wormhole billiard-ball calculations show self-consistency

tellings.quote: physicists in the in the 80s kind of did the math I mean they got interested in wormholes

plain: In the 1980s, physicists who became interested in wormholes, imagined shortcuts through space and time, worked out the math of a billiard ball going through one and running into its own past self. According to Eric Wargo, a writer on precognition, they found that the ball's path could always come out self-consistent. He brings it up without naming a source, as a sign that sending things back in time need not create paradoxes.
